item.title: ZFS Scrub, Resilver, Snapshot, and Replication Solve Different Failure Modes
item.description: A scrub detects latent corruption, a resilver reconstructs missing redundancy, a snapshot preserves an earlier dataset state, and replication puts that state somewhere else. Calling all four 'backup' hides the failures each one cannot solve.

item.title: Wi-Fi CSI Presence Detection Fails First at Calibration, Drift, and Synchronization
item.description: CSI is extremely sensitive to the radio channel—which is why it can sense motion and why uncontrolled rooms, clocks, channels, furniture, fans, and hardware differences can swamp a naive detector.

item.title: Why System of a Down Choruses Often Feel Like Public Speech
item.description: How melody can transform a private line into something that sounds collective

item.title: Why Observability Workloads Keep Ending Up in ClickHouse
item.description: Logs and traces are wide, append-heavy events that are usually filtered by time and a few fields, then aggregated. That workload shape explains the attraction to a columnar analytical database better than any benchmark headline.

item.title: WebRTC Connectivity Is Not “STUN or TURN” — It Is an ICE Candidate Selection Problem
item.description: STUN discovers reachability information and TURN provides a relay, but ICE is the algorithm that gathers candidates, checks candidate pairs, prioritizes working paths, and nominates the connection media actually uses.

item.title: Voice AI Latency Is a Waterfall, Not One Number
item.description: A voice agent can report fast STT, fast LLM, and fast TTS while still feeling slow because endpointing, network boundaries, tool calls, buffering, and playout delays accumulate between those component timers.

item.title: terraform test Is Not terraform validate — and It Can Create Real Infrastructure
item.description: validate checks syntax and internal consistency. terraform test can run plan/apply test cases and assertions, including real provider operations, so it belongs in a different CI risk class.

item.title: Terraform -target Is an Emergency Tool, Not a Deployment Strategy
item.description: Resource targeting narrows Terraform to a selected subset plus dependencies. It is valuable for exceptional recovery but can leave the rest of the configuration unapplied.

item.title: Terraform State Surgery Should Be Rare, Explicit, and Audited
item.description: state mv, state rm, state replace-provider, state pull and state push can change Terraform's ownership model without directly changing remote infrastructure.

item.title: Terraform State Locking Prevents Concurrent Writers, Not Bad Decisions
item.description: State locking serializes writers against one state. It cannot tell whether a plan is destructive, credentials point at the right account, or force-unlock is safe.

item.title: Terraform State Is Not a Cache — It Is the Binding Database
item.description: State maps resource addresses in configuration to real remote objects. Treating it as disposable cache data is how infrastructure gets orphaned or recreated.

item.title: Terraform Stacks vs Workspaces Is a Lifecycle Design Choice
item.description: A workspace manages one root module and one state. HCP Terraform Stacks coordinate multiple components and repeated deployments. The choice is about how many infrastructure lifecycles you need to compose, not which UI looks newer.

item.title: Terraform sensitive Does Not Mean Secret
item.description: Marking a value sensitive redacts normal CLI and UI output. It does not remove that value from Terraform state or saved plan files.

item.title: A Saved Terraform Plan Is a Deployment Artifact, Not Just Pretty Diff Output
item.description: A saved plan captures the exact actions Terraform intends to apply. In CI/CD it becomes the handoff between review and execution—and a sensitive artifact that must be protected.

item.title: Use Terraform -replace When the Object Is Broken but the Configuration Is Right
item.description: Sometimes infrastructure is unhealthy in ways Terraform cannot infer from HCL. -replace makes that one-run replacement intent visible in the plan instead of mutating state ahead of review.

item.title: terraform_remote_state Is a Trust Boundary, Not Just a Convenience
item.description: Reading outputs from another Terraform state is convenient, but consumers generally need access to the full underlying state snapshot. That couples security and deployment boundaries.

item.title: Terraform Provider Upgrades Are Schema Migrations, Not Dependency Chores
item.description: A provider defines resource schemas, planning behavior, defaults, import rules, and state upgrades. Changing its version can alter plans even when no HCL changes, so provider upgrades deserve infrastructure review.

item.title: Terraform Provider Aliases Are Part of a Module's Public Interface
item.description: Provider configurations carry account, region and credential context. A reusable module that needs aliases is declaring runtime dependencies, not merely HCL syntax.

item.title: Terraform Policy Is Not Just Sentinel Rewritten in HCL
item.description: HashiCorp's 2026 Terraform Policy beta evaluates provider-aware infrastructure policies using HCL and a dedicated tfpolicy test workflow. It changes where platform teams can encode guardrails, but it is still beta.

item.title: terraform show -json Is an Automation Interface With a Security Footgun
item.description: The JSON form of a plan exposes structured resource actions, configuration and state for automation. It can also expose sensitive values in plaintext, so policy tooling must treat it as protected data.

item.title: Terraform moved Blocks Are Migration History, Not Cleanup Noise
item.description: A moved block records that a resource address changed while the remote object did not. Removing it too early can make older module consumers see a destructive refactor.

item.title: Module-Level depends_on Can Make Terraform's Graph Much Bigger Than You Think
item.description: A module-level depends_on creates a broad ordering relationship between groups of resources. It can make plans more conservative and hide the specific dependency the system actually has.

item.title: The Terraform Dependency Lock File Is Part of Your Reproducibility Boundary
item.description: required_providers constrains acceptable versions; .terraform.lock.hcl records the exact provider selections and checksums Terraform should install. Committing one without understanding the other creates false confidence.

item.title: Terraform import Blocks Make Brownfield Adoption Reviewable
item.description: Configuration-driven import turns existing infrastructure adoption into code that can be planned, reviewed, repeated, and paired with the resource configuration it will become.

item.title: Terraform ignore_changes Is an Ownership Boundary, Not a Drift Fix
item.description: ignore_changes tells Terraform that selected attributes may be controlled elsewhere after creation. Used casually, it can hide real drift and make configuration stop describing production.

item.title: Terraform for_each Keys Are Resource Identity, Not Loop Variables
item.description: The keys in for_each become part of resource addresses. Renaming a key can look like deleting one object and creating another even when the human thinks only a label changed.

item.title: Terraform Ephemeral Values and Write-Only Arguments Change the Secret-Handling Model
item.description: Terraform 1.10+ ephemeral values and 1.11+ write-only arguments let temporary values pass through a run without being persisted in state or plan artifacts when providers support them.

item.title: Terraform Drift Detection Is Not the Same Thing as Drift Repair
item.description: A normal plan refreshes reality before calculating changes. Refresh-only mode updates Terraform's recorded view without changing infrastructure. The real decision is which side is authoritative.

item.title: Terraform create_before_destroy Can Propagate Through the Dependency Graph
item.description: create_before_destroy changes replacement ordering to reduce downtime, but naming constraints, quotas, dependencies, and temporary double-capacity decide whether that strategy is actually safe.

item.title: Moving Terraform from count to for_each Is a State Migration
item.description: count identities are numeric indexes; for_each identities are keys. Switching syntax without mapping addresses can make unchanged infrastructure look like replacement work.

item.title: Terraform check, precondition, and postcondition Blocks Fail at Different Boundaries
item.description: Terraform has several validation primitives because not every rule should fail at the same time. Preconditions protect assumptions, postconditions protect guarantees, and check blocks report ongoing health without necessarily blocking a run.
